assessments.summary: The packet gives a coherent conditional weak-duality construction and substantially supports the exact invariant tensor identity, but it does not establish the bundled claim. The essential Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 converse, its quantifiers, side conditions, six encoded rows, and permission to fix the auxiliary pair G,K are neither proved nor supplied as declared evidence. The continuous numerical enclosure lacks an objective execution attestation; the claimed zero-intercept negative gap, quotient-coordinate interpretation, and provenance assertions are also not independently verified. No decisive mathematical counterexample is shown.
scopeQualifications: Conditional on the exact tensor audit, the global affine-line inequalities, and applicability of the encoded Theorem 9 rows, the posterior relaxation and weak-duality argument are sound.
The stated K is exactly the input/output reflection of G.
At epsilon = 0.000173428163029, the displayed weights are nonnegative and the coefficients of both R1 and R2 sum algebraically to one.
The binary-input posterior mutual-information identities and the relaxation to mass, mean, and martingale constraints are valid.
Conditional on the certificate inequalities, auxiliary-channel prior coefficients and total affine slope cancel, leaving a concave reflection-symmetric prior bound maximized at q0 = 1/2.
Selecting either branch of a converse bound of the form R <= min{A,B}, and adding a nonnegative side-condition expression to an upper-bound combination, have the correct inequality direction.
The verifier design appears plausibly fail-closed from static inspection, but static inspection does not certify that every interval cell and tiny positive margin passed.
If the stated final enclosure is established, its upper endpoint is below 0.369296945969202842443, so the boxed rounded bound follows.
The asserted final endpoint is strictly below the preceding repaired-certificate value, so strict improvement follows conditional on both numerical certificates.
The repaired source uses the asserted group-b intercept 10^-33; exact zero-backoff feasibility is not established.

The invariant representation is algebraically supported: both combinations have rate vector (1,1), the weights are nonnegative for 0 <= epsilon <= 1/3, paired-row weights agree, the W/U/V tensors match coefficientwise, and the remaining root-level G/K residuals cancel across groups sharing q0.
For the displayed quotient point, the normalization 2s_B+s_C+s_D+s_E=1 follows directly.
The exact functional identity is supported conditional on the encoded row definitions and skew-pairing convention, but the named rank-eight quotient interpretation is not established.
evidenceIssues: No declared reference supplies or proves the precise Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 converse needed for the capacity claim.

The packet does not establish that the six encoded rows faithfully transcribe the external theorem or satisfy its complete intersection/union, hierarchy, auxiliary-channel, and side-condition quantifiers.
Exact-Fraction checks establish consistency of the internally encoded rows and tensor, not their validity as a converse for all achievable private-message rate pairs.
No pinned or objective terminal execution attests the reported PASS result, the 136 interval-cell checks, the very small margins, or the stated high-precision enclosure for U.

The frozen-slope zero-intercept gap is claimed negative only narratively; the repaired verifier visibly checks the positive 10^-33 intercept rather than independently certifying the zero-intercept evaluation.
The map from the six row-pair weights to the named rank-eight quotient coordinates is asserted without a supplied quotient definition or derivation.

The claims that the materials are four accepted artifacts and verbatim or byte-identical copies from specified commits lack judgment records, source-commit byte attestations, hashes, or terminal comparisons.
